text:
Jordan (support): hey folks — ACME Support just escalated a production failure on /v1/rerank/batch. ticket ACME-7832. they say top-k appears shifted across queries after a recent client push :sob:

ACME Support (customer): we're seeing wrong scores. example payload -> model returns items that belong to neighbor query. our ranking is effectively rotated, causing mis-ordering in UI. urgent.

Jordan (support): repro payload pasted below from customer (redacted api_key). note per-query candidate lists are included as separate arrays (they think).

ACME Support (customer): ```json
{
  "queries": [
    {"id":"q1","text":"best raspberries for jam"},
    {"id":"q2","text":"raspberry storage tips"},
    {"id":"q3","text":"how to freeze berries"}
  ],
  "candidates": [
    ["cand_a","cand_b","cand_c"],
    ["cand_d","cand_e"],
    ["cand_f","cand_g","cand_h","cand_i"]
  ],
  "max_results": 3
}
```

Jordan (support): customer says response payload came back as a flat list of scores without clear boundaries and they observed items intended for q2 scored under q1 and so on. copied trimmed server response below.

api-bot: POST /v1/rerank/batch 200 0.47s

Jordan (support): ```json
{
  "results": [
    {"query_id":"q1","ranked": ["cand_a","cand_b","cand_d"],"scores":[0.94,0.88,0.75]},
    {"query_id":"q2","ranked": ["cand_e","cand_f"],"scores":[0.92,0.60]},
    {"query_id":"q3","ranked": ["cand_g","cand_h","cand_i"],"scores":[0.89,0.86,0.80]}
  ]
}
```

Jordan (support): you can see cand_d ended up in q1's list. customer claims this started right after we rolled the batching change last night.

Priya (eng): thanks for the report. pinging @Maia and @Riley. initial hypothesis: boundary encoding/flattening mismatch between client-expected per-query offsets and server flattening (we recently changed delimiter handling for the candidates param).

Riley (ml): can you confirm how client packs candidates? two common shapes: a) nested list (per-query array-of-arrays) or b) flat list + offsets. server expects the latter now for performance. if client still sends nested and we interpret as flat, that would cause shifts.

Jordan (support): customer insists they sent nested arrays (see payload). but our ingress might be normalizing into flat without recomputing per_query_counts.

Maia (eng-oncall): grabbing logs for thread 1963027890. found ingress parser log: 

```
INFO parse_candidates: received candidates as 'array' (type: object)
DEBUG flattening_mode: 'ASSUME_FLAT'
WARN per_query_counts absent -> using cached header offsets: [3,2,4]
```

Maia (eng-oncall): that WARN looks bad. cached header offsets were stale from previous request; we didn't recalc when input shape was mixed. looking into code path in batching layer.

Priya (eng): ok repro locally. I ran the customer's JSON against current master and saw the same rotation. minimal repro below.

Priya (eng): repro script (trimmed):

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://inference.internal/v1/rerank/batch -d @payload.json -H 'Content-Type: application/json' | jq .results
```

Priya (eng): server returned q1 ranked contained cand_d. quick root cause: when candidates are nested, the parser attempts to memoize offsets but uses a stale offsets buffer if the top-level array objects are not homogenous (we accept arrays of arrays or arrays of strings). edge case: if one inner array length matches previous total, it's misinterpreted.

Riley (ml): that explains score misalignment. fix: validate per-query counts after parsing and return 4xx if mismatch instead of silently using cached offsets. also add a schema check that candidates must be either flat+offsets or nested consistently.

Sam (devex): customer impact: ACME is hitting real UX regression (their product shows wrong items). we should offer immediate mitigation steps to customer: 1) ask them to submit flat payload with explicit offsets OR 2) downgrade to previous gateway (roll back) until patch deploy.

Jordan (support): i messaged ACME with mitigation options and offered temporary bypass using our legacy endpoint /v1/rerank/batch?compat=legacy to force the old parser. they're ok with temp fix but want ETA.

Maia (eng-oncall): patch idea: on parse, compute derived per_query_counts from nested arrays and compare to any provided offsets; if mismatch -> 400 + diagnostic. also add unit test for mixed shapes. I can ship a small hotfix to staging within 2 hours.

Priya (eng): I'll prepare the PR. plan: (a) strict validation + explicit error; (b) log the raw request to an S3 debug bucket if validation fails and include short id in error to help repro; (c) add telemetry metric "rerank.nested_shape_errors".

Riley (ml): also check scoring pipeline that consumes flattened candidate vector. if we add strict validation we won't hit the scoring misalignment anymore. still good to add a guard assert in scoring to verify sum(per_query_counts) == len(candidates_flat).

Sam (devex): can we get a short note for docs/SDKs to clarify expected candidate shapes? I'll update quickstart and call out breaking change in the changelog.

Jordan (support): ACME asked if this could be considered a severity 1. not yet total outage but data corruption. we recommended S2 and provided the legacy endpoint.

ACME Support (customer): thanks. legacy endpoint worked and restored ordering. please let us know ETA for fix.

Maia (eng-oncall): ETA: hotfix to staging in ~2h, prod deploy after validation in ~8h if tests pass. will post back when PR is up. assigning to Priya.

Priya (eng): PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rerank/pulls/5427 (draft). patch adds validation and error codes. unit tests added for these shapes. cc @Sam for docs text.

Sam (devex): i'll prep a short advisory and a snippet showing how to convert nested lists to flat+offsets: 
```python
def flatten_candidates(nested):
  flat = []
  offsets = []
  for arr in nested:
    offsets.append(len(arr))
    flat.extend(arr)
  return flat, offsets
```

Sam (devex): will also add note to SDKs and include the legacy-compat flag example.

Jordan (support): marking this thread as "investigating". will update ACME with status and timeline. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Priya (eng): PR ready for review, running CI now. I'll attach reproducible payload and unit test to the PR.

Maia (eng-oncall): PROD deploy window scheduled for 18:00 UTC. I'll monitor post-deploy and notify support channel on completion.

Jordan (support): ACME confirmed they can wait for the fix, appreciate quick turnaround. closing escalation once prod deploy confirmed.

Riley (ml): follow-up action: add a nightly test that randomizes nested vs flat payloads and asserts no alignment errors. adding to backlog.

Sam (devex): after deploy I'll send a short email to customers who might be affected and update the breaking-changes doc.

Jordan (support): thanks all.
